test_cases.test_name: End-to-End Workflow Template Configuration and Execution
test_cases.objective: Verify that the platform can successfully configure and execute a complete personalized therapy workflow template from apheresis through infusion, enforcing chain-of-identity and custody.
prerequisites: System installation is complete
Test workflow template is defined
Test user accounts with appropriate permissions are created
Mock patient and product data is available

test_steps.action: Log into the system using configured SSO credentials and navigate to the workflow template configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and gains access to the workflow configuration interface.

test_steps.action: Configure a new end-to-end workflow template including apheresis, manufacturing slot allocation, QC release, and infusion steps with defined handoff points.
test_steps.expected_result: System saves the workflow template configuration without errors and displays a confirmation message.

test_steps.action: Initiate the configured workflow for a test patient and simulate the apheresis start event with dual-scanning verification of patient identity.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow instance is created successfully and advances to the first step after successful dual-scan verification.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for the start event

test_steps.action: Progress the workflow through manufacturing slot allocation, simulating material handoffs with dual-scanning at each custody transfer point.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow advances through each step, enforcing chain-of-custody verification and recording all handoff events in the audit trail.

test_steps.action: Complete the workflow through simulated QC release and infusion, applying e-signatures for critical release steps.
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow completes successfully with all e-signatures captured, chain-of-identity maintained, and final status recorded.

acceptance_criteria: Workflow template configuration is saved and retrievable without data loss
All dual-scan verification steps are enforced and logged
Complete audit trail is generated for the entire workflow instance
E-signatures are applied and stored compliant with 21 CFR Part 11
Chain-of-identity is maintained throughout the workflow execution
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GDP guidelines for chain-of-custody documentation
GAMP Category 4 for configured systems
data_integrity_requirements: All workflow events must generate immutable audit trail entries
Dual-scan verification must create tamper-evident records
E-signatures must be cryptographically secured
All timestamps must be system-generated and non-modifiable
related_tests: Performance load testing for concurrent workflows

test_cases.test_name: Configurable Risk Scoring and Exception Handling Verification
test_cases.objective: Validate that the system properly executes configurable risk scoring rules and triggers appropriate exception handling workflows for temperature excursions and delays.
prerequisites: Workflow execution capability verified
Risk scoring rules configured
Exception handling workflows defined

test_steps.action: Configure a set of risk scoring rules using the vendor scripting interface to evaluate manufacturing schedule adherence and material quality parameters.
test_steps.expected_result: Risk scoring rules are successfully saved and validated by the system without syntax or logic errors.

test_steps.action: Initiate a test workflow and simulate a manufacturing delay that triggers the configured risk scoring rules.
test_steps.expected_result: System detects the delay event, executes the risk scoring rules, and calculates an appropriate risk score.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature excursion event by injecting mock temperature data that exceeds configured thresholds.
test_steps.expected_result: System detects the temperature excursion, triggers the exception handling workflow, and notifies designated personnel.

test_steps.action: Follow the exception handling workflow through to resolution, applying necessary approvals and documentation.
test_steps.expected_result: Exception workflow guides users through appropriate resolution steps with required approvals and complete documentation.

test_steps.action: Verify that all risk scoring and exception handling events are properly recorded in the audit trail and available on the KPI dashboard.
test_steps.expected_result: Complete history of risk events and exceptions is available in audit trails and reflected accurately on monitoring dashboards.
data_to_capture: Data correlation between events and reporting

acceptance_criteria: Configurable risk scoring rules execute correctly and produce consistent results
Exception handling workflows are triggered automatically upon threshold violations
All exception events generate complete audit trails with appropriate approvals
Risk scores and exception statuses are accurately reflected on monitoring dashboards
Temperature excursion handling complies with GDP requirements
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records
GDP guidelines for temperature excursion handling
GAMP Category 4 for configured business rules
data_integrity_requirements: Risk scoring calculations must be reproducible from audit trail data
Exception events must generate immutable records with timestamps
All threshold violations must trigger immediate system responses
Approval workflows must enforce segregation of duties
related_tests: Integration testing with temperature monitoring systems

test_cases.test_name: Multi-Tenant Data Segregation and Access Control Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that data for different therapy centers or manufacturing sites is properly segregated and access is controlled based on user roles and organizational boundaries.
prerequisites: Platform configured with at least two distinct tenant organizations
User accounts with different roles (e.g., Site A Admin, Site B User, Global Viewer)
Patient journey data created for each tenant

test_steps.action: Log in as a user assigned exclusively to Tenant A with a standard user role.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful, and the dashboard displays only data and workflows relevant to Tenant A.

test_steps.action: Attempt to access a patient record belonging to Tenant B by directly using a known Patient ID from Tenant B in the API or URL.
test_steps.expected_result: System returns a 'Access Denied' or 'Not Found' error, preventing data access.
data_to_capture: Audit log entry for access attempt

test_steps.action: Log in as a user with a global 'Read-Only' role across all tenants.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful, and the user can view patient journeys from both Tenant A and Tenant B, but cannot modify any data.
data_to_capture: Ability to view data from multiple tenants

test_steps.action: As the global user, attempt to perform an action requiring a signature (e.g., confirm a custody handoff) on a Tenant A record.
test_steps.expected_result: The action is blocked, and a permission error is displayed.
data_to_capture: Audit log entry for attempted action

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for a Tenant A event while logged in as a Tenant B admin.
test_steps.expected_result: The Tenant B admin cannot see the audit trail entries for Tenant A events.

acceptance_criteria: Users can only view and interact with data for tenants to which they are explicitly assigned.
Direct object-level access attempts across tenant boundaries are prevented by the system.
Global roles function as designed, allowing cross-tenant viewing without modification rights.
All unauthorized access attempts are logged in the audit trail.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Controls for limiting system access to authorized individuals
GDPR / HIPAA - Requirements for data minimization and access control based on purpose
ISPE GAMP® 5 - Guidance on access control for configured systems
data_integrity_requirements: Tenant segregation must be enforced at the database and application logic levels.
Access control lists must be reliably maintained and enforced for all data objects.
Audit trails must accurately capture the tenant context of all actions.
urs_requirements: URS-028-009: 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures for critical actions (implies access control)
URS-028-014: SSO with OIDC and device identity (supports authentication/authorization)

test_cases.test_name: Vein-to-Vein Dashboard KPI Accuracy and Real-Time Update Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the platform's vein-to-vein dashboard accurately calculates and displays key performance indicators (KPIs) in real-time, reflecting the current state of active patient journeys.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured
Test user with dashboard access permissions is created
At least 50 simulated patient journeys are in various stages of progression (apheresis, manufacturing, transit, etc.)
Known expected KPI values for the test data set are documented

test_steps.action: Access the vein-to-vein dashboard using the test user credentials and navigate to the main KPI summary view.
test_steps.expected_result: Dashboard loads successfully, displaying summary KPIs for vein-to-vein time, release timelines, and other configured metrics.

test_steps.action: Manually calculate the expected average vein-to-vein time, on-time release rate, and current active patient count based on the known test data set.
test_steps.expected_result: Manual calculations are completed, providing a baseline for expected KPI values.

test_steps.action: Compare the manually calculated KPI values with the values displayed on the platform dashboard.
test_steps.expected_result: All displayed KPI values on the dashboard match the manually calculated values within an acceptable margin of error.
data_to_capture: Discrepancies between calculated and displayed values

test_steps.action: Simulate a new event that changes a KPI (e.g., mark a therapy as 'Infused' to complete a journey). Refresh the dashboard and observe the update.
test_steps.expected_result: The dashboard updates within 5 seconds, reflecting the new calculated values for the affected KPIs (e.g., average vein-to-vein time).
data_to_capture: Time from event completion to dashboard update

acceptance_criteria: All key performance indicators on the dashboard are calculated and displayed accurately against the known test data set.
The dashboard updates all affected KPIs in real-time (within 5 seconds) following a state-changing event.
No discrepancies greater than 1% are found between manually calculated and system-displayed values for quantitative metrics.
regulatory_basis: General principle of data accuracy and reliability for clinical decision support.
data_integrity_requirements: Data displayed must be accurate, current, and traceable to source system events.
urs_requirements: URS-028-007: Provide dashboards for vein-to-vein time and release KPIs.

test_cases.test_name: Configurable Risk Scoring Rule Engine Validation with Vendor Scripting
test_cases.objective: To validate that the platform's configurable risk scoring engine correctly executes vendor-supplied scripting rules to calculate and assign risk scores to patient journeys or manufacturing lots.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured
Access to the rule configuration interface
At least 3 pre-written risk scoring rule scripts (e.g., for temperature excursion severity, schedule delay impact, material quality)
Test data sets that will trigger various outcomes for each rule (low, medium, high risk)

test_steps.action: Using the administrative interface, deploy the first pre-written risk scoring rule script (e.g., for evaluating temperature excursions) to the rule engine.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the script configuration and confirms successful deployment without syntax errors.

test_steps.action: Create or modify a test patient journey to include a data point that will trigger the deployed rule (e.g., a logistics event with a minor temperature excursion). Save the record.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes the event and automatically executes the risk rule. A risk score is calculated and assigned to the record.

test_steps.action: Verify the calculated risk score matches the expected output defined in the rule's logic for the given input parameters.
test_steps.expected_result: The assigned risk score is correct based on the script's conditional logic and the input data.

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 1-3 for the other pre-written rule scripts, using test data designed to trigger different risk thresholds.
test_steps.expected_result: All configured rules execute correctly, and the calculated risk scores are accurate and consistent for various test scenarios.
data_to_capture: Results for each rule test iteration

test_steps.action: Attempt to deploy a malformed script with a syntax error and observe system behavior.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the deployment and provides a clear error message describing the script validation failure.

acceptance_criteria: The rule engine successfully executes all deployed vendor scripts without runtime errors.
All calculated risk scores are accurate and consistent with the defined logic of the scripted rules.
The system provides appropriate error handling and clear messages for invalid script configurations.
The audit trail records the execution of risk rules and the resulting score assignments.
regulatory_basis: General principle of automated calculation accuracy and configuration control.
data_integrity_requirements: Risk score calculations must be deterministic, reproducible, and based on accurate source data.
urs_requirements: URS-028-005: Support configurable risk scoring rules using vendor scripting.

test_cases.test_name: Multi-System Data Consistency and Reconciliation Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that data remains consistent across all integrated systems (EHR, LIMS, MES, courier) and that reconciliation processes correctly identify and resolve discrepancies in patient journey data.
prerequisites: Platform configured with workflow templates
Integration connections established with EHR, LIMS, MES, and courier systems
Test patient journeys created with known data patterns
Reconciliation module configured and operational

test_steps.action: Create 10 test patient journeys with specific data points across apheresis, manufacturing, and logistics stages
test_steps.expected_result: Patient journeys are successfully created and distributed across integrated systems

test_steps.action: Intentionally introduce data discrepancies in 3 patient records across different systems (EHR, LIMS, MES)
test_steps.expected_result: Discrepancies are created without immediate system failure

test_steps.action: Execute the automated reconciliation process and monitor for discrepancy detection
test_steps.expected_result: System detects all introduced discrepancies and generates reconciliation reports

test_steps.action: Verify the resolution workflow for identified discrepancies and confirm data consistency restoration
test_steps.expected_result: All discrepancies are resolved and data consistency is restored across all systems

acceptance_criteria: 100% of introduced data discrepancies are detected by the reconciliation process
Reconciliation completes within 15 minutes for 10 patient journeys
All integrated systems show consistent data after resolution
Audit trail captures all reconciliation activities and resolutions
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Electronic records integrity and accuracy
GDP Chapter 4 - Requirements for documentation and record keeping
FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Guidance
data_integrity_requirements: ALCOA+ principles maintained throughout reconciliation process
Immutable audit trail for all data synchronization events
Data provenance tracking across system boundaries
Reconciliation results cryptographically signed
urs_requirements: URS-028-002: Enforce chain-of-identity and chain-of-custody
URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events
URS-028-013: Integrate with EHR, LIMS, MES, courier systems

test_cases.test_name: Custom Algorithm Module Performance Under Peak Load Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that custom algorithm modules maintain required performance characteristics and decision accuracy when processing high volumes of patient matching and risk scoring requests during peak operational loads.
prerequisites: Custom algorithm modules deployed in containerized environment
Performance monitoring tools configured
Load testing framework established
Baseline performance metrics established

test_steps.action: Deploy and configure the custom patient-to-lot matching optimization module with performance monitoring
test_steps.expected_result: Module is operational and performance metrics are being captured

test_steps.action: Generate simulated load of 1,000 concurrent patient matching requests with realistic data patterns
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts all requests without immediate rejection

test_steps.action: Monitor algorithm performance metrics including response time, accuracy, and resource utilization during peak load
test_steps.expected_result: Performance remains within acceptable thresholds throughout the test

test_steps.action: Verify explainability artifacts are generated correctly for all algorithm decisions under load
test_steps.expected_result: All decisions include valid explainability artifacts regardless of load conditions

acceptance_criteria: Average response time remains below 1 second for 95% of requests
Algorithm decision accuracy remains above 99% under peak load
CPU utilization does not exceed 80% and memory usage remains stable
Explainability artifacts generated for 100% of decisions within 2 seconds
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - System performance and reliability requirements
FDA Guidance on Computerized Systems in Clinical Investigations
ICH Q9 - Quality Risk Management principles
data_integrity_requirements: Algorithm decisions must be reproducible under identical inputs
Performance degradation must not compromise decision integrity
Explainability artifacts must remain accurate and complete
All performance metrics must be captured in immutable logs
urs_requirements: URS-028-006: Allow optional custom-developed modules for patient-to-lot matching optimization
URS-028-011: Orchestrate 1,000 concurrent patient journeys
URS-028-012: Event processing latency < 1 second under normal load
URS-028-015: Custom algorithm modules shall be containerized and versioned
URS-028-016: Provide explainability artifacts for algorithm decisions
